text:
Vincent Trocheck is in a new jersey this season, his fourth NHL team, and Utah is using him the way his old teams did: hard minutes and a lot of contact. He has 49 hits in 18 games, a big number for a 5'11" center, and the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette noted the Mammoth have built a Pittsburgh line around him and Logan Cooley.

The points are a little behind: 10 in 18 games, three goals on 9.7% shooting. The underlying play is better than that. Utah has 59% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, and the team has scored about three fewer goals than its chances deserved in his minutes. His ice time has been climbing too, up to 18 minutes a night over the last ten.

The question from last season was defense. Evolving-Hockey had opponents creating more against him than against most forwards, though he also drew the toughest competition in the league. At 33, he's a useful, abrasive second-line center. Our range has him around 53 points, which is about what Utah needs.
headline: Vincent Trocheck brings Pittsburgh grit to Utah
